summary: Jointly trains an answer classifier and a policy for deciding when to defer to a human. Experiments on four short-answer classification tasks show that joint training improves selective prediction and the performance of both components.
imageAlt: Three-stage architecture: warm up the classifier, warm up the deferral policy, then jointly train both using a shared reward signal.

summary: AsRRN models relationships among question contexts, prompts, reference answers, and student responses. Developed with 6,532 statistics responses, it combines recurrent message passing and contrastive learning to assess answers and group them for feedback.
imageAlt: AsRRN diagram showing context, question, reference, and answer nodes passing messages over time to produce an assessment and feedback.

summary: Learns when an automatic short-answer grader should defer to a human using a logistic-regression policy. The study examines how deferral choices balance assessment accuracy with the amount of human grading required.
imageAlt: Sensitivity plot showing assessment accuracy in blue and human deferral rate in red as the deferral penalty increases.

summary: Compares classroom grades with reliable post-hoc assessments of college physics lab reports. The findings motivate paired rubrics: one to communicate expectations to students and a finer-grained version to make grading more consistent.
imageAlt: Box plots of student performance across seven pendulum-report rubric dimensions and eight Newton's second-law report dimensions.

summary: Studies AI-assisted feedback for six short-answer statistics tasks completed by 1,935 students. Human-rating reliability and exploratory response clustering provide a foundation for formative assessment in large-enrollment classes.
imageAlt: Two cross-tabulations compare human reviewers' feedback codes before and after one reviewer removes direct quotations from student responses.

summary: SFRN learns relationships among a question, reference answers, and a student's answer for automatic short-answer grading. Semantic feature-wise transformations combine those relations, while translation-based data augmentation addresses limited and imbalanced training data.
imageAlt: SFRN architecture maps question-reference-answer triples to relation vectors, combines them through semantic feature-wise transformation, and predicts an assessment.

summary: MC-MDP uses reinforcement learning to select question-relevant sentences before extracting an answer. Experiments on MS MARCO show how selecting main content improves downstream reading-comprehension models.
imageAlt: Two plots compare ROUGE-L and F1 for raw documents, golden passages, and MC-MDP across sentence-selection window sizes.

summary: A hierarchical reading-comprehension pipeline first selects passages, then question-relevant sentences, and finally an answer span. The method combines attention-based encoding with a Markov decision process and is evaluated on DuReader search data.
imageAlt: Pipeline from question, titles, and passages through passage selection, main-content selection, and answer extraction to the final answer.

summary: A visual dataflow system lets users build, run, monitor, and reuse machine-learning workflows as directed acyclic graphs. It connects a drag-and-drop studio with algorithm libraries and Hadoop/Spark infrastructure, including both standalone and distributed operations.
imageAlt: System architecture with a machine-learning studio above the algorithm library and big-data infrastructure for scheduling, computation, and data management.

summary: A semi-supervised language model incorporates sentiment labels into word-vector learning. Evaluated on English and Chinese product reviews, the approach studies how semantic and sentiment information can jointly support review classification.
imageAlt: Classification-accuracy curves for English and Chinese reviews across word-vector dimensions and sentiment-weight settings.
